purpose: library: the five atmospheric layers as comparable categories ordered by altitude, identified by thermal characteristics, chemical composition, movement and density and bounded by 'pauses' — exosphere (about 375 to 6,200 miles; atoms escape, satellites orbit; thermopause below), thermosphere (53-375 miles; upper atmosphere; UV and x-ray absorption raising temperature from as low as -184°F (-120°C) to as high as 3,600°F (2,000°C) yet feeling cold; mesopause below), mesosphere (31-53 miles; meteors burn up; stratopause below), stratosphere (4-12 to about 31 miles; 19 percent of the atmosphere's gases; ozone formation heating from -60°F (-51°C) to about 5°F (-15°C); temperature inversion preventing convection; tropopause below) and troposphere (surface up to 11-12 miles at the equator, 5½ miles at 50°N/S, under 4 miles at the poles; almost all weather; temperature dropping from around 62°F (17°C) to -60°F (-51°C)). Fits a compare table of layer × altitude range × temperature behaviour, quiz cards with predict-then-reveal on the ranges and the 19 percent figure, and step ordering from the ground up.
